problems.theorem_title: The conditional interpolation and analytic determinant argument for pi
problems.formal_statement:
theorem OAI.PiExponent.DeterminantContradiction.piEventualLowerBound_of_interpolation_and_analytic_aggregate
    (hgeometry : GlobalInterpolationStatement) (hanalytic : AnalyticAggregateStatement) :
    PiEventualLowerBound := by
  sorry
problems.natural_language_statement:
Assume the global interpolation statement and the analytic aggregate statement for the original fixed admissible data. Then, for every real $\nu>2$, there is an integer $Q\ge2$ such that every $p\in\mathbb Z$ and $q\in\mathbb N$ with $q\ge Q$ satisfy

$$q^{-\nu}\le\left|\pi-\frac pq\right|.$$

This is the conditional conclusion of the source determinant contradiction, with the original quantified interpolation and analytic hypotheses.

problems.theorem_title: Global surjectivity of the original admissible interpolation matrix
problems.natural_language_statement:
For every real $\nu>2$, every fixed admissible datum $d$, and every real lower height $L$, the original interpolation matrix $A_d(H)$ is surjective at some height $H\ge L$:

$$\forall\nu>2\;\forall d\;\forall L\in\mathbb R\;\exists H\ge L,\quad\operatorname{Surjective}(A_d(H)).$$

Here the matrix, its weighted row and column domains, and the fixed-data parameters are exactly those of the source global interpolation statement.

problems.theorem_title: The original analytic aggregate bound for admissible selected minors
problems.natural_language_statement:
For every real $\nu>2$ and fixed admissible datum $d$, there is an error $e_d(H)\to0$ as $H\to+\infty$. Eventually, every selected minor $D$ with nonzero determinant satisfies

$$\frac{\log\|\det D\|}{M_d(H)H}\le a_d+e_d(H)+\max\{-\gamma_d(H),-\nu[A_d(1-\eta_d)-b_d(H)]\}.$$

Here $M_d(H)$ is the row count, $a_d$ the analytic error parameter, $\gamma_d(H)$ the collision rate, $A_d$ and $\eta_d$ the fixed-data parameters, and $b_d(H)$ the normalized weighted row mean. The bound is uniform over the original column selections and is precisely the source analytic aggregate statement.
